migrationCompatibility.notes: Drops two policies and creates none. The stable release connects as postgres and is exempt from RLS, so it is unaffected either side of the migration; a candidate connected as juli_app is strictly better off. Both tables keep four per-command policies, and the migration asserts that coverage BEFORE dropping rather than trusting it.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: downgrade recreates both policies exactly as migration 001 left them, including the one-argument current_setting. The downgrade restores the prior state faithfully rather than a corrected version of it — a downgrade that silently improves things hides what the upgrade changed.

acceptanceCommands: DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres@localhost:5432/<freshly-created> JULI_TEST_DATABASE_DISPOSABLE=1 PYTHONPATH=$PWD/backend/src:$PWD python -m pytest tests/integration/test_migrations.py tests/integration/test_rls_policies.py tests/integration/test_two_tenant_isolation_proof.py -q
psql -At -c "select policyname from pg_policies where tablename in ('shops','users') order by 1"
doNotInfer: Do not require a policy for all four commands on every RLS-enabled table. production_write_audit is append-only by design — migration 047 says 'no UPDATE or DELETE grants. SELECT/INSERT only for juli_app' — so its missing policies are intended denial. A first version of this test asserted four commands everywhere and failed on it; the pressure that creates is to add policies that widen access.
Do not correct the one-argument current_setting in downgrade(). The downgrade must restore migration 001's policies exactly, defect included, or the upgrade becomes unreviewable.

Do not pattern-match on '%_isolation' to find policies to drop. Migration 045 already dropped seventeen of them legitimately; a pattern would silently widen if another arrives. The two triples are named explicitly.

Do not conclude the deployed system is affected today. It connects as postgres, the table owner, which is exempt from RLS — which is exactly why three waves of CI never saw this. Verify as juli_app or not at all.
Do not verify by reading the migrations. All three W7 grant/policy omissions had correct-looking source and a database that disagreed; read pg_policies.
